items.title: Randomized procedures as probability kernels
items.statement:
Let $\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$
be a statistical experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]) and let
$(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$ be a measurable **action space**: a set of available
actions equipped with a sigma-algebra of action events, hence a measurable
space ([[def-measurable-space]]). A **randomized procedure** (or
randomized decision rule) is a probability kernel $K$ from
$(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ to $(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$, in the pointwise sense
of [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]. Thus $K(x,\cdot)$ is a
probability measure on $(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$ for every $x\in\mathcal X$,
and $x\mapsto K(x,B)$ is $\mathcal A$-measurable for every $B\in\mathcal G$.
After observing $x$, the procedure assigns probability $K(x,B)$ to taking an
action in $B$. The kernel is specified without reference to the unknown
parameter. This definition imposes no measurable structure on $\Theta$. The
kernel is the specification of the procedure; no representation by a separate
random seed is asserted for arbitrary measurable action spaces.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§2–4.2, PDF pp. 2–8
Peter Kempthorne, MIT 18.655 Lecture Note 6: Sufficiency, PDF pp. 14–15

items.title: A randomized procedure has a measurable action law
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a randomized procedure for the experiment
$\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$
with action space $(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$. Give $[0,+\infty]$ its Borel
sigma-algebra. For every nonnegative $\mathcal G/\mathcal B([0,+\infty])$-
measurable function $g:\mathsf D\to[0,+\infty]$, the function
$$h_g(x)=\int_{\mathsf D}g(a)\,K(x,da)$$
is $\mathcal A$-measurable. In particular, $x\mapsto K(x,B)$ is measurable
for every action event $B\in\mathcal G$. For each $\theta\in\Theta$, the
set function
$$Q_\theta(B)=\int_{\mathcal X}K(x,B)\,P_\theta(dx),\qquad B\in\mathcal G,$$
is a probability measure on $(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$, and for every such $g$,
$$\int_{\mathsf D}g\,dQ_\theta=\int_{\mathcal X}\left(\int_{\mathsf D}g(a)\,K(x,da)\right)P_\theta(dx).$$
with nonnegative extended values allowed.
items.strategy: Use increasing simple approximations and pointwise monotone convergence to prove measurability of integration against the supplied kernel. Normalize the action law, prove countable additivity by monotone convergence of finite event sums, establish the iterated-integral identity for indicators and simple functions, then pass to all nonnegative measurable functions by monotone convergence.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§2–4.2, PDF pp. 2–8

items.title: Statistics and estimators
items.statement:
Let $\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$
be an experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]). A **statistic** with target
measurable space $(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ is a measurable map
$T:(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\to(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$, where measurability
means that $T^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal A$ for every $B\in\mathcal B$
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). If
$\psi:\Theta\to\mathcal Y$ is an estimand ([[def-estimand-on-a-statistical-model]])
and its target set $\mathcal Y$ is equipped with $\mathcal B$, a statistic
$\widehat\psi$ with this same target space is an **estimator of $\psi$**.
The value $\widehat\psi(x)$ is the estimate at observed data $x$. Giving
$\mathcal Y$ a measurable structure is an additional choice; this definition
does not assert that $\psi$ is measurable as a function of the parameter.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §2, PDF pp. 2–3

items.title: Randomized tests
items.statement:
A **randomized test** is a randomized procedure with binary action space
whose action set is $\{0,1\}$, equipped with its full sigma-algebra
$2^{\{0,1\}}$ (the power set, which is a sigma-algebra by
[[def-sigma-algebra]]), where $1$ means reject and $0$ means do not reject
([[def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel]]). Its **test function** is
$$\varphi(x)=K(x,\{1\}),\qquad x\in\mathcal X.$$
Since $K(x,\cdot)$ is a probability measure and $\{0\},\{1\}$ partition the
action set, $K(x,\{0\})+K(x,\{1\})=1$. Thus $\varphi(x)\in[0,1]$ and
$1-\varphi(x)=K(x,\{0\})$ is the probability of not rejecting. Give $[0,1]$
the trace of the Borel sigma-algebra on $[0,+\infty]$, namely
$\{C\cap[0,1]:C\in\mathcal B([0,+\infty])\}$. By
[[lem-procedure-action-law-is-measurable]], $x\mapsto K(x,\{1\})$ is
measurable; since it has range in $[0,1]$, its preimage of $C\cap[0,1]$ equals
its preimage of $C$ and is measurable for every such $C$. Hence $\varphi$ is a
measurable map in the preimage sense of
[[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]. Its value is the
rejection probability after observing $x$.
The convention $1=\text{reject}$ is fixed here. No null or alternative
hypothesis is part of this definition.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §5.1, PDF pp. 100–102
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §3, PDF pp. 4–5

items.title: A deterministic statistic is a Dirac kernel
items.statement:
Let $T:(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)\to(\mathcal Y,\mathcal B)$ be a statistic in
an experiment. Define
$$K(x,C)=\delta_{T(x)}(C)=\begin{cases}1,&T(x)\in C,\\0,&T(x)\notin C,\end{cases}\qquad C\in\mathcal B.$$
Then $K$ is a randomized procedure that assigns probability one to the
statistic value $T(x)$ after observing $x$.
items.strategy: Verify pointwise that the Dirac section is a probability measure. For each measurable action event, its kernel evaluation is the indicator of the measurable preimage under T.

items.title: A coin-flip randomized test
items.statement:
Let the data space be the one-point space $\mathcal X=\{x_0\}$ with its full
sigma-algebra, let $\Theta=\{\theta_0\}$, and take
$P_{\theta_0}=\delta_{x_0}$. For any $p\in[0,1]$, define a binary procedure by
$$K(x_0,B)=p\,1_{\{1\in B\}}+(1-p)\,1_{\{0\in B\}},\qquad B\subseteq\{0,1\}.$$
It is a randomized test with rejection probability $p$.
items.strategy: Check the four binary action events to verify a probability measure and the one-point kernel measurability condition. Integrate the rejection evaluation under the point-mass data law to obtain p, including p=0 and p=1.

items.title: A nonmeasurable rule is not a statistic or test
items.statement:
Every set map from a statistical data space to the binary action space is a
statistic or a randomized test function.
items.strategy: Construct a one-parameter experiment on the trivial sigma-algebra, then show the preimage of the measurable rejection event {1} is not measurable. Apply the statistic and test definitions to refute the claim.
